Two panels illustrating inductance. Left panel (Self-Inductance): A single coil of wire wrapped around a core, connected to a battery and a switch. Magnetic field lines expand around the coil, with an arrow showing an induced "back e.m.f." pointing opposite to the battery current. Right panel (Mutual Inductance): Two separate coils placed side by side. The primary coil is connected to a battery and switch; the secondary coil is connected to a galvanometer. Expanding magnetic field lines from the primary coil cut through the secondary coil. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Two circuit diagrams showing inductors. Top diagram (Series): Three coiled symbols representing inductors labelled L₁, L₂, and L₃ connected end-to-end in a single line. Bottom diagram (Parallel): Three inductor symbols connected in separate parallel branches, with the branches meeting at common junctions on the left and right. Labels L₁, L₂, and L₃ on each branch. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Two panels comparing solid and laminated metal cores in a changing magnetic field. Left panel: A solid rectangular block of metal showing large, circular, swirling eddy currents (thick circular arrows) inside it, with a label "Large eddy currents = High heat loss". Right panel: A similar block sliced into thin vertical sheets (laminations) separated by thin insulating layers. Inside each thin sheet, much smaller, narrower eddy current loops are shown, with a label "Small eddy currents = Low heat loss". Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
